correctness.rationale: Each of the two voter arcs has a unique absorbing recurrent interface class; a positive-rate path from every state reaches it. Independent arc interfaces have detailed balance pi_{i+1}/pi_i=beta/alpha and generate the exact convolution and its two tails. Strict positive convexity of x/(1-r^{-x}) at r>1 reverses at r<1; normalization-product differences have strict positive sign for all r>0, a+2<=b. Boundary cases r=1, arc length one, and n>=4 are explicit. Exact rational full-generator tests are reproduced by verify.py and certificate.json but not treated as universal proof.

value.rationale: The motivated zealot-placement problem has a complete strictly ordered, all-size, all-bias answer whose optimum abruptly reverses at symmetric persuasion. The two extreme outcomes become jointly more likely under zealot clustering even as the favored camp mean rises, an interpretable tradeoff for opinion design and risk. This is not merely a parameter substitution or computational one-off; the global strict convexity and tail identities drive nontrivial comparative statics.
